rejections.title: Evidence dated after the analysis
rejections.meaning: Future information would leak into the analysis, so the context is refused before the debate starts.

rejections.title: Required data unavailable
rejections.meaning: The system abstains: it will not guess from data it does not have.

rejections.title: Required domain missing
rejections.meaning: Unknown is escalated to review, never treated as neutral.

rejections.title: All domains available
rejections.input: all five domains report a value
rejections.meaning: Only this outcome lets the run reach the model.

rejections.title: Proposal the validator refuses
rejections.meaning: The model's proposal is never published: deterministic code decides, not the prose.

rejections.title: Overwriting a final decision
rejections.input: write a second decision with the same record id
rejections.meaning: Records are append-only. A revision must be a new record that points at the old one, so the history stays readable.

rejections.title: Budget exhausted
rejections.meaning: The call is refused before it reaches the provider.

governance.title: Agent opens a pull request
governance.detail: The coding agent writes the module, its tests and the documents.

governance.title: CI catches what local runs cannot
governance.detail: Two source files carried a UTF-8 BOM. On Linux, ast.parse rejected them, so all four Python versions failed. The local suite could not run at all (missing runtime dependencies), so CI was the only place this could surface.

governance.title: Review and CI catch what the agent missed
governance.detail: Each module had something the first pass did not. A review found that adding a new log entry had also rewritten a historical governance record. For B, replaying a real trace showed a cap above the baseline still degrading the run (BUG-004). For the integration, a signature change broke an older test the CI never collected. None of these came from the agent reporting its own mistake.

governance.title: Agent fixes, reviewer re-checks
governance.detail: The historical entry was restored verbatim and the diff against main now shows an addition only. A second round caught a canonical stage name falling through to the default stage.

governance.title: Green, approved, merged
governance.detail: Eight checks pass on four Python versions and the reviewer approves.

decisions.question: Who decides if a proposal is legal?
decisions.chosen: Deterministic code. The model proposes; a validator accepts or rejects.
decisions.rejected: Letting the model judge its own proposal, or trusting prose that claims safety.
decisions.because: A model that can write "this trade is safe" can also write it when it is not.

decisions.question: What does missing data mean?
decisions.chosen: Three states: available, unavailable, unknown. Neutral is a value, never a status.
decisions.rejected: Treating a missing feed as a zero, which reads as a neutral signal.
decisions.because: The baseline run recorded five missing feeds as neutral. That is how an outage becomes an opinion.

decisions.question: What happens when the budget runs out?
decisions.chosen: A fixed degradation ladder, so the run still produces a decision.
decisions.rejected: Stopping the run when a cap is hit, which trades a cost problem for a missing answer.
decisions.because: The first version compared the remaining budget with fixed fractions and degraded a run that fit (BUG-004); the projection form fixed it.

decisions.question: Can a claim stand without evidence?
decisions.chosen: A strong claim must bind to a retrieved unit, dated no later than the analysis date.
decisions.rejected: Publishing the debate as prose and hoping the reader notices which lines are guesses.
decisions.because: A forecast can never be evidence-backed, so it is labelled a hypothesis rather than removed.

A.name: Evidence-grounded debate
A.question: Can a claim be made without evidence?
A.answer: No. A strong claim must bind to a retrieved evidence unit, and the evidence must not be dated after the analysis date.
A.refuse: A claim without evidence is demoted to a hypothesis, or the turn abstains.

B.name: Run budget
B.question: What bounds the cost of a run?
B.answer: A metered ledger: reserve before the call, settle after it, refuse past the cap.
B.refuse: Past the cap the call is refused; below the cap the run degrades along a fixed ladder instead of dying.

C.name: Deterministic simulation safety
C.question: Who decides whether a trade proposal is legal?
C.answer: Deterministic code, not the model. The model proposes; the validator accepts or rejects.
C.refuse: A proposal without a holdings snapshot, with units <= 0 for a buy, or beyond cash is rejected.

D.name: Data sufficiency
D.question: What does it mean when the data is not there?
D.answer: Three states, not two: available, unavailable, unknown. Neutral is a value, not a status.
D.refuse: unavailable abstains; unknown escalates to review. Neither is ever treated as a neutral signal.

stage.label: Data admitted before any model call

E.name: Verifiable audit
E.question: Can a finished decision be trusted later?
E.answer: An append-only hash chain, a supersede chain for revisions, and an offline gate replay.
E.refuse: Overwriting a final decision is rejected; a broken chain fails verification.
